raw:
By the time Ashworth dismisses the orientation, the fourth bell is still fading over the quadrangle.

A glass-fronted slate beside the dueling grounds carries the day’s public schedule. Near the bottom, a fresh line reads:

*Fifth Bell — Ashara vel Kothren, Rank 1 / Iven Rook, Rank 4*  
*Practice weapons. Wards active.*

The octagon is already gathering a ring of students along its low rail. You find a place with a clear view just as Ashara steps onto the packed earth in a sleeveless dark training coat, her practice blade resting against one shoulder. Heat gives the air around her forearms a faint shimmer.

Her opponent is a lean third-year with dark fur visible over his wrists and a split practice staff in hand. He rolls one shoulder, then tests the staff’s balance.

An instructor at the edge of the ring raises one hand. “Three clean touches. No strikes above the collar. No forcing the ward.”

The bell sounds.

Iven moves first, low and fast. His staff snaps toward Ashara’s knee; she turns it aside, but the return sweep catches the padded side of her coat before she can clear it.

“One to Rook,” the instructor calls.

Rashid stands farther along the rail, arms folded over his Conclave coat. He says nothing.

Ashara resets without looking toward him or the crowd. On the next exchange, she gives ground twice, then steps inside the staff’s reach. Her blade taps Iven’s shoulder before he can recover.

“One each.”

Iven’s pace quickens. He presses her toward the ward-line, staff cutting short, efficient arcs through the air. Ashara blocks high, then low; the impact of metal on metal makes the boundary wards flash pale blue. A narrow orange glow runs along her blade near the guard.

When Iven lunges again, she catches the staff against her hilt, twists it aside, and strikes his ribs with the flat.

“Two to Kothren.”

A few people at the rail murmur. Iven grins once, breathes through his nose, and comes in harder.

The final exchange is brief. He feints toward her injured side, commits to the opening he thinks he has made, and Ashara pivots clear. Her tail braces against the earth for an instant as she turns. The practice blade lands cleanly against the center of his chest.

“Bout to Kothren. Three to one.”

The spectators break into scattered applause. Iven lowers his staff and gives Ashara a short bow.

“You heated the blade,” he says.

“You reached too far,” Ashara replies, taking a cloth from the instructor to wipe the grip.

Rashid claps once, then steps away from the rail as the next pair of students begin preparing to enter. On the slate beside the ground, an assistant changes nothing beside Ashara’s name: she remains first.
